title: Choose the look for the Oversight home screen (dark mode)
question: Shown in dark mode, the way the app opens. The roll assigned Colour Field Poster. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Whatever you choose is built in BETA only.

options.label: Colour Field Poster
options.thesis: Each company is a flat field of colour, and its number is the poster.
options.viewport: Cobalt rail, deep ink-navy work area. Each company column opens on a solid colour field carrying its name and today's cash in giant numerals; sections sit below on dark panels under 1px rules.
options.risk: Loud if the fields spread past the column headers; the dark panels below must stay calm.

raised.raise: Every table is set on 1px hairline rules with small uppercase labels, ink never pure black.
Every ranked row draws a bar whose length is its exact value, so size reads before the number does.
All company columns share one fixed chart scale, so Pupik and Monkeytime bars compare honestly.
One period control drives every panel at once, with a live readout of what it is showing.

options.label: Bilingual Wayfinding
options.lineage: Israeli highway and city road signs
options.thesis: Hebrew over Latin on a green shell, read at a glance like a sign at speed.
options.viewport: Sign-green rail and header with white lettering on a near-black green ground; every section title is a two-line Hebrew/Latin pair, and trends are yellow arrow chips.
options.risk: Familiar and safe: green and white can read as a banking app if the yellow arrows are not used sparingly.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: airport boarding pass and departures board
options.thesis: A ranked board where a changed row holds one alert colour until you have seen it.
options.viewport: Dark graphite shell; agent and client lists are ranked rows in a fixed column grid, and rows that changed since the last sync hold amber.
options.case: Holds clarity: ranked rows that show change in place are what the agent and client lists already are. Identification is thinner, since flight boards are universal, not this trade.
options.risk: Dark and technical; can feel cold next to the group's colourful goods.

options.label: Character Roster
options.thesis: Agents and brands as a ranked roster of rounded name plates, one ribbon colour per company.
options.viewport: Deep plum ground; pastel name plates glow against it, one ribbon colour per company, agents ranked as plates with a bar and their cash.
options.case: Holds identification: the group sells character goods, so a ranked, ribbon-coloured roster is its own catalog. Loses clarity where pastel grounds weaken number contrast.
options.risk: Playful: may feel too light for the owner's debt and cost screens, though pastel plates read well on dark.

options.label: Design Annual Plates
options.case: Fuses poorly: a print-annual feel does not identify with a wholesale trading team, and registration marks add decoration to a working screen.
options.kept: Hairline 1px rules and small uppercase labels.

options.label: Dance Score
options.case: Fuses poorly: a vertical mirrored staff is not how anyone here reads sales, and it hides the numbers.
options.kept: Length is exact value: bar length equals the number.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.case: Fuses poorly: cream plates and engraved italics are the default look, and the subject has nothing to do with plants.
options.kept: Compared panels share one fixed scale.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.case: Fuses poorly: giant letterforms leave no room for the tables people read here.
options.kept: One control drives every panel, with a live readout.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean dark analytics dashboard: slate cards, one blue accent.
canonCard.viewport: Slate sidebar, KPI cards on a deep navy ground, standard charts and tables.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
